org.portico.bindings.jgroups.wan.local

Class Bundler

  • java.lang.Object
    • org.portico.bindings.jgroups.wan.local.Bundler

  • public class Bundler
extends Object
    This class is responsible for sending all messages to the WAN router. It will bundle a number of messages together to ensure efficient use of network resources and enable higher throughput. This class handles all message sending. ## Bundling As messages are received, they are stored until one of two trigger conditions is met: - The size of the bundled messages exceeds a configurable threashold - The amount of time we have been holding onto messages exceeds a configurable threshold To ensure a balance between throughput and latency, we will only hold onto messages for a certain amount of time. At this point they will be flushed to the router, even if the combined size of the messages is less than our bundling limit. If a message is submitted that causes the bundled size to exceed the threshold, the submit(byte, UUID, byte[]) method notifies the dedicated sender thread, which then calls flush(), sending all the messages to the router. This will cause the call to `submit()` to block until that flush is complete. This helps throttle the sender somewhat to prevent overloading. ## Disable Bundling Although the default behaviour of this component is to bundle messages, it is also the main interface to the WAN router. When required, the actual bundling of the messages can be turned off, causing every messaegs to be flushed to the WAN router as soon as the call to submit(byte, UUID, byte[]) is made. See setBundling(boolean).

    • Method Detail

      • submit

        public void submit(byte header,
                   UUID sender,
                   byte[] message)
        Submit a message for bundling. If the size limit is now broken, a flush will happen and this method will block. Otherwise it will return. If this is the first message since the last flush, the timer will be armed so that if our size cap isn't broken in a configurable amount of time (20ms by default), a flush will happen anyway. This method will block in two instances: - If the total size of bundled messages exceeds the limit, causing a flush - If a flush is already under way #### Disable Bundling Bundling can be disabled in configuration. If this is the case, submitted messages will immediately be flushed to the router.
